title: A waiter can roll a started bar item back to 'yeni' and void it without approval, hiding the after-send void
description: setItemsStatus allows any status change, backwards included, for anyone with siparis.al; garson has no mutfak.ekran. Setting status 'yeni' clears startedAt, readyAt and servedAt. voidItem decides 'fresh' (no approval, severity info, voidAfterSend false) from status === 'yeni' && !startedAt && createdBy === actor && within the 2-minute grace window (line 343). So once the bar has started an item, the waiter who added it can POST /kitchen/status {status:'yeni'} and then void it with no siparis.iptal approval. The audit records it as a harmless fresh void and the kitchen waste is not counted (voidAfterSend false).
evidence:
void after bar started (no approver) -> 403 approval_required
garson POST /kitchen/status yeni -> 200
void after reset (no approver) -> 200
item row { voided: true, voidApprovedBy: null, voidAfterSend: false }
audit [ { severity: 'info', approverId: null, data: { afterSend: false, fresh: true } } ]
fix: Restrict backward transitions, especially to 'yeni', to users with mutfak.ekran, and keep startedAt when rolling back (or store a separate firstStartedAt). Base the voidItem 'fresh' check on 'never started' (e.g. firstStartedAt == null), not on the current status.

I ran it on its own with `npx vitest run --config .../verify-state-r1-reproduce/vitest.probe.config.mts rollback-void`, and all 4 checks failed against the correct behaviour.

Output:
- A: after the bar sets the item to hazirlaniyor (startedAt set), the waiter's void without an approver gets "403 approval_required". Then "garson reset -> 200 status yeni startedAt null" and "void after reset -> 200 { voided: true, voidApprovedBy: null, voidAfterSend: false }". The audit row reads severity 'info', approverId null, data { afterSend: false, fresh: true }.
- B: the same happens when the bar has already marked the drink 'hazir': "B reset 200 void 200 { voided: true, voidApprovedBy: null, voidAfterSend: false }".
- C: computeSummary gives "voided 58500 voidAfterSendCount 0", so the day report does not count these voids as after-send waste.
- D: the same bypass works on whole-order cancel (cancelOrder, orders.ts:1041 allFresh): "cancel before reset 403 approval_required ; after reset 200 { voidApprovedBy: null, voidAfterSend: false }".

Root cause:
- setItemsStatus (orders.ts:1074-1100) only requires mutfak.ekran OR siparis.al, and the garson role has siparis.al (shared/permissions.ts:68).
- It accepts any target status, including going back to 'yeni', and that clears startedAt, readyAt and servedAt.
- It writes no audit row for the rollback.
- The kitchen UI (src/pages/KitchenPage.tsx) never sends status 'yeni', so only a direct API call can do this. The UI is not a legitimate route to it.
- voidItem's fresh check (line 343: status==='yeni' && !startedAt && createdBy===actor && within VOID_GRACE_MS) is therefore defeated, and afterSend (line 345) is computed from the current status.

This breaks the project rules on server-side permission checks and on auditing sensitive actions: the void is logged as a harmless fresh void, and the after-send waste count is lost.

Limiting factors, which keep this at medium rather than high:
- The void must come within 2 minutes of the item being sent.
- The actor must be the waiter who added the item.
- A manager approving a void after a rollback would also record afterSend=false.

Confirmed. My probe shows the waiter can void even a drink the bar has already served, with no approval.

- "garson POST /kitchen/status yeni -> 200" (garson has only siparis.al; the role list in shared/permissions.ts has no mutfak.ekran)
- "after garson reset { status: 'yeni', startedAt: null, readyAt: null, servedAt: null }" (the served drink's history is wiped)
- "garson void after reset, no approver -> 200"
- "row { voided: true, voidApprovedBy: null, voidAfterSend: false }"
- "audit [ { severity: 'info', approverId: null, amount: 39000, data: { afterSend: false, fresh: true } } ]" (amount is 390 TL in kuruş)
- "any audit for the kitchen status rollback? 0"
- "day summary voided / voidAfterSendCount 39000 0" (the Z line "İptal (N hazırlandıktan sonra)" undercounts)
- The assertion expect(voided.status).toBe(403) fails with 200.

Why this is a bug and not intended:
- In setItemsStatus (server/services/orders.ts:1074-1097), anyone with siparis.al can set any status, including going backwards. Setting 'yeni' clears startedAt, readyAt and servedAt.
- voidItem (line 343) decides an item is 'fresh' from the current status ('yeni' and no startedAt). So the reset turns a served item into a free void that is logged as info.
- docs/00-GELISTIRILMIS-PROMPT.md lists an acceptance rule: "Garsonun gönderilmiş kalem iptali yetkili PIN'i olmadan yapılamaz; yapılınca patron panelinde uyarı çıkar". That says a waiter cannot void a sent item without a manager PIN, and the patron panel shows a warning when it happens. Both parts are broken here: no approval, and severity info instead of uyari/alarm.
- AGENTS.md rule 3 says permissions are enforced on the server and hiding things in the client is only a convenience. So "the UI never sends this" does not excuse it.
- The 'yeni' value has no legitimate caller. KitchenPage's "Geri al" and the history-item tap send only 'hazirlaniyor', and no test posts status 'yeni'. Restricting it would not break any UI flow.

What limits the impact (why medium, not high):
- It needs a direct API call with the waiter's own session.
- It only works on items that waiter added, within VOID_GRACE_MS (2 minutes) of sending.
- The bar still gets a ticket.void event.
Still, espresso drinks are often made and served within 2 minutes. This is the classic void-and-pocket-cash fraud that the approval rule exists to stop, and it leaves no approver, no warning and no waste count.

The proposed fix is sound. Allow moving items back to 'yeni' only with mutfak.ekran (or drop 'yeni' from the API enum, since nothing uses it). Keep a first-started timestamp, and base the 'fresh' check on "never started". The same fresh logic in cancelOrder at line 1041 has the same weakness.

- "garson reset served item to yeni -> 200"

That means the bypassed void is hidden from any uyari/alarm audit filter. The status rollback itself writes no audit row ("status-change audits 0"). Because voidAfterSend is false, the bar screen does not show the crossed-out cancelled line either.

Cause: setItemsStatus (server/services/orders.ts ~1094) lets anyone with siparis.al set any status, including 'yeni'. Setting 'yeni' clears startedAt. voidItem's 'fresh' check (line 343) then passes. The same 'fresh' logic is in cancelOrder (line 1041).

- Only the 2-minute VOID_GRACE_MS window after sending counts, and only for the waiter's own items.
- The UI has no way to set 'yeni' (KitchenPage only moves forward, or back to 'hazirlaniyor' from history). The waiter would have to send crafted API calls with their bearer token.
- The bar still hears the iptal beep and sees the item jump back to waiting.
- The void amount still appears in the Z voided total and as an info audit row.

Real effect: a free or comped drink that bypasses approval and is misreported as a harmless fresh void, and a wrong after-send count on the Z. It is a server-side permission bypass, but narrow.

title: Void-approval requirement bypassed by rewinding kitchen status to 'yeni'
description: voidItem treats a void as 'fresh' (no siparis.iptal approval, audit severity 'info', voidAfterSend=false) when it.status==='yeni' && !it.startedAt && createdBy===actor && now-sentAt<2min. setItemsStatus (reachable via POST /api/kitchen/status by anyone with mutfak.ekran OR siparis.al) allows setting status back to 'yeni', which also nulls startedAt/readyAt/servedAt. So a garson can let the bar prepare and serve an item, rewind its status to 'yeni' to clear startedAt, and then void it with no approver and no alarm as long as the original sentAt is still within the 2-minute grace window — defeating the rule that a sent/prepared item needs yetkili onayı and masking it in the audit log.
fix: Base the 'fresh' decision on whether the item was ever started/served, not on the current (rewindable) status: persist a first-sent/was-prepared marker and compute fresh from that, or forbid setItemsStatus from moving an item back to 'yeni' for non-privileged callers. Keep voidAfterSend/severity driven by whether the kitchen ever worked the item.

title: Replayed or double-submitted amount and item payments are recorded twice and close the order with only half collected
description: addPayment has no idempotency key and no expected version or remaining check for 'Tutar' (amount) and 'Kalem' (item-selection) payments. Two identical concurrent or replayed requests both succeed. A half-amount cash payment sent twice records two payments and closes the order, though the customer handed over half; expected cash is overstated. An item payment of 1 of a 2-unit line sent twice charges both units. Share payments are already guarded for exactly this case (shareNo plus amount must match, comment at line 854: 'yanıtı kaybolan istek yeniden geldiyse'), but the other two modes are not.
fix: Accept a client-generated idempotency key (e.g. a requestId stored unique on payments) and return the original result on replay. Or require the client to send the order version / remaining it saw, and reject with 409 when it no longer matches, as the share path does.

The behaviour reproduces on the current code. I wrote my own probe at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-reproduce/replay.probe.test.ts. I ran only that file with the given vitest config. All 3 duplicate cases failed the correct-behaviour assertions, and the share-path contrast passed.

Output:
- A (half cash, two concurrent identical POSTs): statuses [200,200], order status "kapali", payments [14000,14000], paid 28000 of total 28000. Expected cash (GET /cash/day as patron) rose by 28000, though the cashier sent half once.
- B (half cash, sequential replay as after a lost response): statuses [200,200], status "kapali", payments [14000,14000].
- C (Kalem mode, 1 of a 2-unit line, sent twice): statuses [200,200], paidQty "2/2", payments [14000,14000], order closed.
- D (Paylaş replay with the same shareNo): statuses [200,409,"split_changed"], order still "acik" with 1 payment (output in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-reproduce/replay-D.log).

Cause: addPayment in server/services/orders.ts (around lines 835-940) takes no idempotency key and no expected version or remaining for the Tutar and Kalem modes. Each request runs in its own SQLite write, so the second one sees remaining = half. It then passes the `amount > remaining` check and closes the order. The Kalem path recomputes paidQty from the current row, so the replay takes the other unit.

The trigger is realistic on the client:
- src/lib/api.ts does not retry on its own. But when fetch throws, it reports status 0 ('network').
- act() in src/pages/order/useOrder.ts invalidates the order only on 409. After a lost response the modal therefore keeps the same amountText (or item selection), and pressing Pay again sends an identical body.
- The Button loading state blocks double taps on one device, but not this lost-response retry, and not two devices taking the same table.

The authors already guard exactly this case for shares (comment at line 854: 'yanıtı kaybolan istek yeniden geldiyse'), so this is a gap in their own design. The 'full' case is protected only because nothing is left to pay (nothing_due / order_closed).

Mitigations that keep this at medium rather than high:
- A legitimate second identical payment (two diners each paying half) cannot be told apart from a replay without a client key, so the fix needs a client-generated request id or the client's view of remaining.
- A wrong payment can be undone with an approved refund.

Impact: the order closes with half collected, expected cash is overstated (in blind-cash mode the cashier cannot see this), and a card record can disagree with the terminal.

Confirmed. A payment request repeated after its response was lost gets recorded a second time in 'Tutar' (amount) and 'Kalem' (item) modes. The project already guards this exact case for share payments: server/services/orders.ts:854-856 and the test at tests/split-bill.test.ts:100 ("Yanıtı kaybolan istek yeniden gelir: ikinci kez pay alınmaz"). So the expected behaviour comes from the project's own rule. It is not invented.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-correctness/dup-replay-verify.probe.test.ts (log in dup-replay-verify.log in the same folder). It sends the same body twice in a row, mirroring the project's share test, and fails on Tutar and Kalem:
- share replay [200,409,"split_changed"] -> payments 1, order still open (guarded)
- tutar replay [200,200,null,true] -> status kapali, payments 2, paid 28000 of total 28000, customerHandedOver 14000, expectedCashDelta 28000. Expected cash goes up by 280 TL while only 140 TL went into the drawer.
- kalem replay [200,200,null,true] -> payments 2, paidQty 2 of qty 2, so both units are charged for a 1-unit selection.
- control: two guests each paying half, with the screen refreshed in between, still succeeds [200,true]. This shows the fix must be a client-sent idempotency key or the expected paid/version (the proposed fix). Blindly dropping identical bodies would block legitimate payments.

How this happens in practice: the client has no automatic retry (src/main.tsx mutations retry 0), and the Pay button is disabled while busy. So a concurrent double tap like the original Promise.all probe cannot happen from the UI, and "double-submitted" overstates it. The real path is a lost response. In src/lib/api.ts a fetch failure throws status 0 ("Sunucuya ulaşılamadı"). useOrder.act only shows a toast; it refetches only on 409. PaymentModal.pay returns before resetting, so the amount, method and selection stay on screen. When the cashier presses Öde again, the identical body is sent, the server accepts it, and the UI shows "Adisyon kapandı".

Result: the order closes while a guest still owes their half. Expected cash or card totals are overstated, and under blind cash the cashier cannot see this; it surfaces as a shortage at the Z count. It can be undone by a payment refund (odeme.iade approval, same day only), which writes an alarm-level audit entry.

Severity is medium: the outcome is silent money misstatement in a POS, and the project already treats this scenario as one worth defending. It is borderline low, because it needs a network failure in the window after the commit plus a manual press again.

The server behaviour is real. The realistic trigger is much narrower than the claim says, so I rate it low, not medium.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/replay.probe.test.ts. Log: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/replay.log. The probe sends each request twice in a row, the way PaymentModal would resend after a lost response; they are not sent at the same time. Output:
- A (half cash, retried): `{"r1":200,"r2":200,"r2closed":true,"total":28000,"handedOver":14000,"status":"kapali","payments":2,"paid":28000,"expectedCashDelta1":14000,"expectedCashDeltaTotal":28000}`. The order closes with half still owed. Expected cash goes up by 280 TL although only 140 TL was handed over, so the Z count will show a 140 TL shortage. With blind cash, the cashier cannot see this before the count.
- C (card payment for 1 of a 2-unit line, retried): `{"r2":200,"status":"kapali","payments":2,"paidQty":2,"qty":2,"paid":28000}`. The second unit is marked paid and the order closes, so the second payer is never asked to pay.
- For comparison, B (share payment replayed) gets `409 split_changed` with 1 payment, and D (full payment replayed) gets `409 order_closed`.
Failing assertions: order status expected 'acik', got 'kapali'; expected-cash change expected 14000, got 28000; paidQty expected 1, got 2.

Why it is low, not medium:
1. The PaymentModal pay button is disabled while the request is in flight (Button sets `disabled={disabled || loading}`, and pay() calls setBusy(true) before its first await). A double tap on one device cannot send two requests.
2. src/lib/api.ts never retries automatically. withApproval only resends after a 403 approval_required, and that rejection happens in needDirect before anything is written.
3. Writes are synchronous single SQLite transactions. Two identical requests from two devices are just two cashiers each taking half, which the server must allow. So the original probe's concurrent case is not a bug by itself.

The one real path: the server commits, then the response is lost (for example a phone changes Wi-Fi network, ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED). The cashier sees "Sunucuya ulaşılamadı", the modal keeps the same amount and item selection, and the cashier taps pay again. The server accepts it.

This is the same lost-response replay the share path already guards against (comment near orders.ts:854, "yanıtı kaybolan istek yeniden geldiyse"). The Tutar and Kalem modes have no such guard.

How visible it is:
- When the replay closes the order, the result screen says "Adisyon kapandı" instead of "Kalanı al". The payment list shows two identical payments seconds apart, and a same-day refund with approval can fix it.
- When the replay does not close the order (for example, one of three people paying), there is no visible signal and the café quietly collects less.

The harm is real money lost or misreported, but it needs a rare network failure in a narrow window.

title: An order-level discount silently covers items merged or transferred in (a garson can make another table's bill free)
description: The order discount is stored on the order (discountType/discountValue) and is applied by calcFor to whatever items the order holds at recalc time. mergeOrders and transferItems move items into a target without re-checking the target's discount. They do not call discountApproval and write no order.discount audit. A garson (masa.islem, no siparis.indirim) can therefore move a full-price bill into an order that has a manager-approved 50% or 100% discount, and the moved items become discounted or free. The only audit trail is the original approval for one coffee.
evidence:
source total before merge 140000 target total 7000 target discount 7000
merged: gross 154000 orderDiscount 77000 total 77000
audited discount amounts on target: [ 7000 ]
before: source 84000 target 0 → after transfer: source 0 birlesti target 0 target orderDiscount 98000
AssertionError: expected 77000 to be 147000 / expected +0 to be 84000
fix: When mergeOrders or transferItems would grow the effective discount of an order that has discountType set, refuse with 409 or require a new discountApproval for the resulting amount and write an order.discount audit. Alternatively, convert the order discount to its approved absolute amount when it is approved, so new items are not covered by it.

The bug reproduces on the current code. Control (passed): a garson asking for a 100% order discount directly, with no approver, gets 403. So garson really lacks siparis.indirim.

Merge: I made a 1-coffee order and the mudur approved a 100% discount on it ('İkram'). A separate 10-coffee order on another table had a total of 140000. The garson called POST /orders/:id/merge with no approverPin and got 200. Output: "MERGE after: gross 154000 orderDiscount 154000 total 0". The only new audit row was 'order.merge:null'. The only order.discount audit on the target is still [14000]. The garson then closed the order with POST /close: "MERGE close status 200 status kapali total 0". So the garson turned a 1400 TL bill into free and closed it, and the audit trail only records a 140 TL discount. Failing assertion: "expected +0 to be 140000".

Transfer: I made a 1-coffee order and the mudur approved 50%. The garson transferred 6 coffees (84000) into it and got 200. Combined totals went from 91000 to 49000: "TRANSFER after: source 0 birlesti target 49000 target orderDiscount 49000". The order.discount audit on the target is still [7000]. Failing assertion: "expected 49000 to be 91000".

Neither re-checks discountType/discountValue on the target, calls discountApproval, or writes an order.discount audit. setOrderDiscount stores the percent itself and audits only the amount at approval time, so recalc/calcFor applies the percent to whatever items arrive later.

This breaks the rule that sensitive actions like discounts are audited, and it causes direct revenue loss through a role that is denied discount permission. I kept severity at high.

The root cause is wider than merge and transfer. The stored order discount is a live percent, so items added later with POST /items are covered too, as the original probe's first case shows. A fix in merge/transfer alone would miss that path.

The mechanics reproduce, but the expected behaviour in the claim is wrong for this project. This is how a percentage bill discount is meant to work, and the merge path gives a garson nothing they can't already do.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-money-r1-correctness/order-discount-merge-verify.probe.test.ts (4/4 pass). Output:
- A, merge into a 50% target: "target before 7000 source before 140000 -> merged gross 154000 orderDiscount 77000 total 77000", "effective pct 50", audits [order.merge:null, order.discount:7000].
- B, baseline: a garson simply ADDS the same 10 coffees to the 50%-discounted order, using only siparis.al and no approval. Result: "gross 154000 orderDiscount 77000 total 77000", the same as the merge, with the same single order.discount:7000 audit.
- C, the indirim report (/reports/items?kind=indirim) shows "Adisyon indirimi value 77000 reason Personel by Müdür". That is the live full amount, not the 7000 at approval time.
- D, transfer into a 100% target: "source 84000 -> 0 birlesti; target 0 -> 0 orderDiscount 98000". The effect is the same as adding items to a 100%-discounted (fully comped) bill.

Why this is not a bug:
(1) The order discount is a percentage rule on the whole bill. shared/order-calc.ts calcOrder applies percentOf to the current subtotal on every recalc, and docs/04-YAZARKASA.md §5 describes items added after a discount and the discount being spread again. A Turkish café expects a %10 student or %20 staff discount to cover the second round too.
(2) Approval is checked against a percentage, not an amount. discountApproval compares pct with maxDiscountPct. After the merge the effective discount is still exactly the approved 50% (probe A), so no approval limit is exceeded.
(3) addItems on a discounted order (needDirect siparis.al, server/services/orders.ts:229) already lets a garson put any number of items under the manager-approved percentage. mergeOrders and transferItems (lines 577, 609) open no new permission path. Requiring re-approval only on merge or transfer would protect nothing.
(4) It is not silent. The merge or transfer is audited (order.merge / order.transfer, with approverId from masa.islem). The indirim report and the Z discount totals (reports.ts:106/287/341, days.ts:131) read the live totals.orderDiscount with reason and approver, so the patron sees the real 770 TL.

The only quirk is that the order.discount audit row keeps the amount at approval time. That is informational, and the reports carry the true figure.

The proposed fix ("refuse 409 / re-approve on merge") would also break normal table joins under a legitimate percentage discount. Turning the percentage into a fixed amount at approval would break the documented re-distribution behaviour.

The bug is real. My probe reproduces it, and it has money impact.

- Output: `KASA merge status 200 owed before 147000 (A 7000 + B printed bill 140000) → merged total 77000 orderDiscount 77000`
- The kasiyer then records 77000 cash and the order closes (`paid 77000 closed true status kapali`).
- `order.discount audits on A: ['7000/uyari']`. No new approval, and no new order.discount audit entry.
- The discount report row `#2 Adisyon indirimi 77000 Personel by=Müdür` credits the manager with 770 TL, though they approved 70 TL.

**Garson transfer.** Table B's 6-coffee bill (84000) is transferred by a garson, with no PIN, into a check with a manager-approved 100% discount:
- Output: `B before 84000 → B 0 birlesti | A 0 → 0 orderDiscount 98000`
- The kasiyer can then close A at 0 (status 200).

**Impact:**
- **Permission bypass:** masa.islem alone extends a discount to another table's already-entered bill. Granting a discount needs siparis.indirim.
- **Money loss:** the customer can be handed the full printed bill while the till records the discounted amount. Blind cash expects only what was recorded, so the count matches and the skim is hidden.
- **Misreporting:** the audit log and the patron alert feed show only the small approved discount, and the discount report credits the inflated amount to the approving manager.
- **Accidental loss:** it can also happen by mistake. Merging a joining group into a staff or owner's-guest discounted table silently discounts their whole bill.

**Why medium, not high:**
- It only works when an open check already has a manager-approved percent discount. Amount-type discounts are capped, so they do not grow.
- The Z report and the discount report still show the full discount total, so it is not hidden from after-the-fact review. The `order.merge`/`order.transfer` audit rows also exist for anyone who checks.
- Adding items directly to a discounted check gets the same discount (`ADDITEMS gross 98000 orderDiscount 98000 total 0`). That suggests a floating percent discount is partly by design. What merge and transfer add is a way to absorb an existing, already-billed table without an approval or a discount audit entry, which breaks the rule that sensitive actions are audited.

title: An amount discount stores the uncapped requested value, so items added later are absorbed beyond the approved and audited amount
description: setOrderDiscount computes the effective amount as min(subtotal, value) for approval and audit, but stores the raw requested value in discountValue (here 1,000,000 kuruş = 10,000 TL). calcOrder caps it to the current subtotal at each recalc. The order therefore keeps an unused discount balance, and every item added later (by anyone with siparis.al) is discounted up to 10,000 TL with no further approval or audit. In the probe the audited discount was 140 TL, but after five more coffees the real discount was 840 TL and the total stayed 0.
evidence:
after discount: total 0 orderDiscount 14000 stored discountValue 1000000
after adding 5 more coffees: gross 84000 orderDiscount 84000 total 0
audited discount amounts: [ 14000 ] [ 'Garson #1 adisyona ₺140,00 indirim yaptı (%100, Misafir)' ]
AssertionError: expected 84000 to be 14000
fix: For type 'amount', store the capped value (the `amount` that was approved and audited: Math.min(subtotal, value)) instead of the raw input.

I ran it alone with a filename filter, because the shared probe directory holds other verifiers' files.

Code path: in server/services/orders.ts, setOrderDiscount (around lines 489-499) does three things:
- It works out `amount = Math.min(subtotal, value)` and `pct` from the current subtotal.
- It uses that amount for discountApproval and for the audit row.
- It saves the uncapped `value` to orders.discountValue.

At each recalc, shared/order-calc.ts:96 caps the order discount again with `Math.min(subtotal, disc.value)`. Any unused part of the stored value therefore stays live and soaks up items added later.

Probe output:
- **Case A** (1 Türk kahvesi = 14000 kuruş; garson asks for a 50000 kuruş amount discount, approved with the mudur PIN): after the discount, gross is 14000, orderDiscount 14000, total 0 and discountValue 50000. After the garson adds 3 more coffees, gross is 56000, orderDiscount 50000 and total 6000. The only audit row is 14000, 'Garson #1 adisyona ₺140,00 indirim yaptı (%100, Misafir)'. The test fails with "expected 50000 to be 14000". The audited discount is 140 TL; the real one is 500 TL.
- **Case B** (stronger variant; amount discount of 1,000,000 kuruş on an empty order): the request returns 200. Because subtotal is 0, amount and pct are both 0, so the approver is asked to approve a 0% discount and the audit records ₺0. After the garson adds 4 coffees, gross is 56000, orderDiscount 56000 and total 0. The only audit row is 0, 'Garson #2 adisyona ₺0,00 indirim yaptı (%0, Misafir)'. The test fails with "expected 56000 to be +0". The whole bill is free, and the audit shows a ₺0 discount.

This breaks the project rule that sensitive actions are audited, and the approval check (pct against maxDiscountPct) never sees the discount that actually applies. Only siparis.al is needed to add items after the discount is set.

Severity medium fits: an approval PIN is still needed once at the start, but the audited and approved amount understates the real discount, by any amount up to the raw value. The proposed fix should close it: save the capped amount, and better still reject an amount discount when the subtotal is 0.

In this project, approval is checked as a percentage (maxDiscountPct), not as an amount. setOrderDiscount approves pct = min(subtotal, value) / subtotal. When the requested value is at least the subtotal, that is 100%, so only someone with a 100% limit can approve it (in the demo seed only mudur and patron; garson and kasiyer do not have siparis.indirim at all). When items are added later, the effective rate is min(S', V) / S', which stays at or below the approved rate. The approval limit is never exceeded on a check that grows.

The audit row recording the discount at the moment it was applied is not specific to amount discounts. Percent discounts are stored as a percent and recomputed when items are added; docs/04-YAZARKASA.md expects items to be added after an order discount and the discount to be redistributed.

title: A per-item payment ignores the client's amount and silently records a different sum when the order changed in between (card terminal mismatch)
description: For items payments, addPayment overwrites the amount with the server's amountForItems result and never compares it with input.amount. The client sends the amount it showed the cashier, and that amount was typed into the bank card terminal. Share payments reject such a mismatch with 409 split_changed, so the wrong amount does not reach the card terminal. Item payments have no such check. If another device changes the order first (here the 50% discount is removed), LafPOS records 140 TL on card while the terminal charged 70 TL. The item is marked paid and the card Z total no longer matches the bank.
evidence:
client charged on card terminal 7000 → server status 200 recorded amount 14000
AssertionError: expected false to be true
fix: In the items branch, compare Math.trunc(input.amount) with Math.min(expected, remaining). If they differ, throw 409 (for example 'items_changed') so the client refreshes before charging, as the share path does.

title: maxDiscountPct cap is bypassed by stacking a line discount and an order discount
description: discountApproval() checks each discount's percentage against actor.maxDiscountPct in isolation. A cashier with siparis.indirim and maxDiscountPct=10 cannot apply a single 19% discount (correctly refused, approval_required), but can apply 10% on an item AND 10% on the whole order with no approver, yielding ~19% effective off the order. Neither setItemDiscount nor setOrderDiscount considers the already-applied discounts when enforcing the cap, so the per-staff discount limit (and the 'kukla hesapla sınırsız indirim olmasın' intent) is defeated by composition. This also understates audit severity, since each leg stays under alertDiscountPct.
evidence:
[discount] single 19% order discount -> 403 approval_required
[discount] line 10% -> 200 ; order 10% -> 200 ; gross 14000 total 11340 effective discount % 19.00
FAIL: expected effective discount (19) <= maxDiscountPct (10).
fix: Enforce the cap on the order's total effective discount, not per-leg: when applying any discount, compute (gross - total)/gross including existing line and order discounts and require approval once the cumulative percentage exceeds the actor's maxDiscountPct (and the approver's, as discountApproval already does for a single leg).

title: Item-based payment marks complimentary and voided lines as paid, so a line that later becomes due cannot be paid by item or voided
description: addPayment checks only that the selection's total value (expected) is above 0. It then sets paidQty on every selected line, including complimentary or voided lines that contribute 0 kuruş. Sending a comped line together with a priced line marks the comped line paid although nothing was collected for it. When the comp is undone (compItem undo does not check paidQty), the line is due (140 TL) but has paidQty=1. Paying it by item returns 'Seçilen kalemler ödenmiş', voiding it returns 'Ödenmiş kalem iptal edilemez', and ÖKC baskets skip it.
evidence:
[PROBE] items after pay [{"name":"Türk kahvesi","complimentary":true,"qty":1,"paidQty":1,"unitPrice":14000},{"name":"Latte",...,"paidQty":1}]
[PROBE] after uncomp {"total":33500,"paid":19500,"due":14000,"line":{"complimentary":false,"qty":1,"paidQty":1}}
[PROBE] pay the now-due line by item 400 Seçilen kalemler ödenmiş ya da ücretsiz
[PROBE] void the now-due line 409 Ödenmiş kalem iptal edilemez; önce ödemeyi iptal edin
AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0
fix: In the selection loop, reject (400) or skip lines that are voided, complimentary, or have lineNet 0, and never write paidQty for them. In compItem undo, refuse when paidQty > 0 or reset it.

title: Unknown or duplicate foreign ids reach SQLite constraints and return 500
description: Several writes insert client-supplied ids without checking they exist, so FOREIGN KEY or UNIQUE errors become 500 'Beklenmeyen bir hata' instead of 404/422. This affects POST /orders customerId (any garson), POST /customers/:id/addresses (customers.ts:121), and POST/PATCH /reservations tableId (reservations.ts:56/71). On the admin side it affects POST /admin/tables sectionId, POST /admin/categories stationId, and POST/PATCH /admin/products stationId/categoryId. PUT /admin/products/:id/groups fails for an unknown product and for duplicate groupIds (admin.ts:149).
fix: Check that each referenced row exists, the way updateOrder already checks customerId, and throw notFound(). Dedupe groupIds and check that the product exists in the groups PUT. As a backstop, map SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_* in app.onError to 409/422.

title: Counter option maxQty is checked per pick; repeating the same pick bypasses it
description: resolveOptions checks maxQty separately for each entry in the client's pick list of a 'counter' group and never merges repeated itemIds. Extra shot has maxQty 1, and one pick of qty 2 is refused. Twenty picks of qty 1 are accepted: 20 shots are sold, 1,000 TL of options are added to a 195 TL Latte, and the bar ticket lists '+1 shot' twenty times.
fix: In the counter branch, sum qty per itemId before validating against item.maxQty, and emit one SelectedOption per item. Also apply the group's maxSelect.
